results.title: Automaticity of automorphism groups of free groups (Farb's Question 7.3)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The statement that for every natural number $n > 3$ the automorphism group $\mathrm{Aut}(F_n)$ of the free group $F_n$ on $n$ generators is an automatic group.

results.title: The spectrum of a group (Kourovka 12.84)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The spectrum of a group $G$ is the set $\{\operatorname{ord}(g) : g \in G\}$ of the orders of its elements, where an element of infinite order is counted as having order $0$.

results.title: Syskin's question on groups with a given spectrum (Kourovka 12.84)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The proposition that for every set $\Omega$ of natural numbers, if two non-isomorphic finite groups both have set of element orders $\Omega$, then for every natural number $k$ there are $k$ pairwise non-isomorphic finite groups whose set of element orders is $\Omega$; that is, infinitely many.

results.title: Two isospectral finite groups do not force infinitely many
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There are a set $\Omega$ of natural numbers and a natural number $k$ such that two non-isomorphic finite groups have set of element orders $\Omega$, but there are no $k$ pairwise non-isomorphic finite groups whose set of element orders is $\Omega$.

results.title: Spectrum of a group (Kourovka 13.63)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a group $G$, the spectrum $\pi_e(G)$ is the set of orders of elements of $G$, where an element of infinite order counts as having order $0$.

results.title: At most $k$ isomorphism types with spectrum $\Gamma$
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a set $\Gamma$ of natural numbers and a natural number $k$, this property holds when, for any finite groups $G_0, \dots, G_k$ (not necessarily distinct) whose spectra $\pi_e(G_i)$ (the sets of orders of elements of $G_i$) all equal $\Gamma$, there are indices $i \ne j$ with $G_i \cong G_j$.

results.title: Infinitely many isomorphism types with spectrum $\Gamma$
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a set $\Gamma$ of natural numbers, this property holds when, for every natural number $n$, there are $n$ pairwise non-isomorphic finite groups $G_0, \dots, G_{n-1}$ whose spectra $\pi_e(G_i)$ (the sets of orders of elements of $G_i$) all equal $\Gamma$.

results.title: Local word identities in connected groups (Kourovka 18.71)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The statement that for every connected Hausdorff topological group $G$ and every word $W(x, y)$ in the free group on two generators $x$, $y$, if $W(a, b) = 1$ for all $(a, b)$ in some nonempty open subset of $G \times G$, then $W(a, b) = 1$ for all $a, b \in G$.

results.title: Local word identities need not hold globally in connected groups
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There are a connected Hausdorff topological group $G$, a word $W(x, y)$ in the free group on two generators $x$, $y$ and a nonempty open subset $U$ of $G \times G$ such that $W(a, b) = 1$ for all $(a, b) \in U$ but $W(a, b) \ne 1$ for some $a, b \in G$. This answers Kourovka Notebook Problem 18.71 in the negative.

part.title: Monochromatic symmetric subsets of abelian groups

path: Monochromatic symmetric subsets of abelian groups

results.title: Monochrome symmetric subsets (Kourovka 15.77)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The statement, written additively, that for every infinite abelian group $G$, every cardinal $\alpha < |G|$, every natural number $n$ and every colouring $\chi \colon G \to \{0, \dots, n - 1\}$, there are a set $A \subseteq G$ of cardinality $\alpha$ on which $\chi$ is constant and an element $g \in G$ such that $2g - a \in A$ for every $a \in A$; that is, $A$ is a monochrome set symmetric with respect to $g$.

results.title: Monochromatic symmetric subsets in finite colourings (Jayadevan)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be an infinite abelian group, written additively, let $\alpha$ be a cardinal with $\alpha < |G|$, and let $n$ be a natural number. For every colouring $\chi \colon G \to \{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ there are a set $A \subseteq G$ of cardinality $\alpha$ on which $\chi$ is constant and an element $g \in G$ such that $2g - a \in A$ for every $a \in A$.

results.title: Geometric points detect elements when the generic fiber is reduced
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: An element of a torsion-free algebra that vanishes under every algebra homomorphism into an algebraically closed field is zero, provided the tensor product with the fraction field is reduced and finite.

results.title: Counting algebra homomorphisms from an étale algebra
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Over an algebraically closed field, the number of algebra homomorphisms from an étale algebra to the base field equals its rank.

results.title: Counting algebra homomorphisms of a finite reduced algebra
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A finite reduced algebra over an algebraically closed field has `finrank` many algebra homomorphisms to the field.

results.title: A tensor vanishing at all pairs of algebraic points is zero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If the scalar-extended evaluation map is injective, a tensor vanishing at all pairs of selected algebraic points is zero. The algebra and the point index may be infinite; no closedness or perfection assumption is needed.

results.title: Algebra maps from relation-preserving generator assignments

results.title: Extending a ring character via prime-subfield-valued linear forms

results.summary: A ring character extends to the algebra generated by another ring image when its kernel contains the first kernel and a separating family of linear forms takes prime-subfield values on that image.

results.title: Lifting maps to algebraically closed fields along integral extensions

results.summary: A homomorphism from `R` to an algebraically closed field extends to an integral extension `S` with any prescribed prime kernel lying over `ker χ`.

results.title: Relation holding triplewise on a set
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $r$ be a ternary relation on a type $\alpha$ and let $s \subseteq \alpha$. The relation $r$ holds triplewise on $s$ if $r(x, y, z)$ holds for all pairwise distinct $x, y, z \in s$.

results.title: Sets with no three collinear points
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A set $A$ of points in the plane is non-trilinear if no three distinct points of $A$ lie on a common line.

results.title: Sets with no $n$ collinear points
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A set $S$ of points in a Euclidean affine space has no $n$ collinear points if no subset of $S$ consisting of exactly $n$ points is collinear.

results.title: Sets containing a convex $n$-gon
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ contains a convex $n$-gon if there is a set $S \subseteq P$ of exactly $n$ points that is convex independent: no point of $S$ lies in the convex hull of the other points of $S$.

results.title: Counterclockwise convex polygons
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $P$ be an oriented two-dimensional Euclidean affine space. Points $p_0, \dots, p_{n-1} \in P$ form a counterclockwise convex polygon if for all indices $i < j < k$ the oriented angle $\measuredangle p_i p_j p_k$ at $p_j$ has sign $-1$, that is, $p_i, p_j, p_k$ are not collinear and lie in counterclockwise order with respect to the orientation of $P$. Every list of at most two points qualifies.

results.title: Convex polygons
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Points $p_0, \dots, p_{n-1}$ of an oriented two-dimensional Euclidean affine space form a convex polygon if one of the lists $p_0, p_1, \dots, p_{n-1}$ and $p_0, p_{n-1}, p_{n-2}, \dots, p_1$ is a counterclockwise convex polygon: for any three of its entries $q, r, s$, in the order in which they occur in that list, the oriented angle $\measuredangle q r s$ at $r$ has sign $-1$. Thus for $n \ge 3$ the points are the…

results.title: Affinely independent triples are convex polygons
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If three points $A, B, C$ of an oriented two-dimensional Euclidean affine space are affinely independent, then $A, B, C$ form a convex polygon.

results.title: Oriented triangle area
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\omega$ be the area form of the given orientation of the Euclidean plane, so that $\omega(u, v)$ is the signed area of the parallelogram spanned by the vectors $u$ and $v$. For points $a$, $b$, $c$ of the plane, the oriented area of the triangle with vertices $a$, $b$, $c$ is the real number $\omega(a - c, b - c) / 2$.

results.title: Maximum number of distinct distance counts
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite set $X \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ and a point $x \in X$, let $R_X(x)$ be the number of distinct distances $\lvert y - x \rvert$ from $x$ to the points $y \in X$ other than $x$. For $n \in \mathbb{N}$, $g(n)$ is the maximum, over all sets $X \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ of exactly $n$ points, of the number of distinct values among the numbers $R_X(x)$ with $x \in X$.

results.title: Points in general position
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A set $X \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$, finite or infinite, is in _general position_ if no three distinct points of $X$ are collinear and no four distinct points of $X$ lie on a common circle.

results.title: Right-angled triangles
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Points $a, b, c$ of a Euclidean affine space are the vertices of a right-angled triangle if they are pairwise distinct and the unoriented angle at one of the three vertices equals $\pi / 2$: $\angle bac = \pi / 2$, $\angle abc = \pi / 2$ or $\angle bca = \pi / 2$.

results.title: Isosceles trapezoids
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Points $a, b, c, d \in \mathbb{R}^2$ are the vertices, in counterclockwise order, of an isosceles trapezoid if they are in strictly convex position and listed counterclockwise (for any three of them $p, q, r$, in the order in which they occur in the list $a, b, c, d$, the oriented angle $\measuredangle p q r$ at $q$ has sign $-1$), the line through $a$ and $b$ is parallel to the line through $c$ and $d$ (the two…

results.title: Isosceles-free sets
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A set $A$ in a space with a distance function $d$ is isosceles-free if there are no three distinct points $x, y, z \in A$ such that two of the distances $d(x, y)$, $d(y, z)$, $d(z, x)$ are equal.

results.title: General position of affine points
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $k$ be a division ring and $P$ an affine space over $k$. A family $(p_i)_{i \in \iota}$ of points of $P$ is in general position through dimension $d \in \mathbb{N}$ if for every finite set $S \subseteq \iota$ of at most $d + 1$ indices, the subfamily $(p_i)_{i \in S}$ is affinely independent over $k$.

results.title: Affinely independent families are in general position
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If a family $(p_i)_{i \in \iota}$ of points of an affine space over a division ring $k$ is affinely independent over $k$, then it is in general position through dimension $d$ for every $d \in \mathbb{N}$.

results.title: General position in affine space is monotone in the dimension
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $d \le e$ be natural numbers. If a family of points of an affine space over a division ring $k$ is in general position through dimension $e$, then it is in general position through dimension $d$.

results.title: General position of projective points
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $k$ be a division ring and $V$ a vector space over $k$, with projective space $\mathbb{P}(V)$. A family $(p_i)_{i \in \iota}$ of points of $\mathbb{P}(V)$ is in general position through dimension $d \in \mathbb{N}$ if for every finite set $S \subseteq \iota$ of at most $d + 1$ indices, the subfamily $(p_i)_{i \in S}$ is projectively independent.

results.title: Projectively independent families are in general position
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If a family $(p_i)_{i \in \iota}$ of points of the projective space $\mathbb{P}(V)$ of a vector space $V$ over a division ring $k$ is projectively independent, then it is in general position through dimension $d$ for every $d \in \mathbb{N}$.

results.title: General position in projective space is monotone in the dimension
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $d \le e$ be natural numbers. If a family of points of the projective space $\mathbb{P}(V)$ of a vector space $V$ over a division ring $k$ is in general position through dimension $e$, then it is in general position through dimension $d$.

results.title: Convex position threshold
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $k$ and $n$, $f_k(n)$ is the least natural number $m$ such that every set of $m$ points of $\mathbb{R}^k$ in general position (any at most $k + 1$ of them affinely independent) contains $n$ points in convex position (none of them in the convex hull of the others). If there is no such $m$, then $f_k(n) = 0$.

results.summary: For natural numbers $k$ and $n$ let $f_k(n)$ be the least $m$ such that every set of $m$ points of $\mathbb{R}^k$ in general position (any at most $k + 1$ of them affinely independent) contains $n$ points in convex position (none of them in the convex hull of the others), with $f_k(n) = 0$ if there is no such $m$. path: Spectral theorem for compact self-adjoint operators

results.title: Eigenvalues are bounded by the operator norm
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $T$ be a bounded linear operator on an inner product space over $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. Every eigenvalue $\mu$ of $T$ satisfies $|\mu| \le \|T\|$.

results.title: Finiteness of large eigenvalues of a compact self-adjoint operator
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $T$ be a compact self-adjoint operator on a Hilbert space over $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. For every $\varepsilon > 0$, the set of eigenvalues $\mu$ of $T$ with $\varepsilon \le |\mu|$ is finite.

results.title: A nonzero compact self-adjoint operator has an eigenvalue of modulus equal to its norm
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $T \neq 0$ be a compact self-adjoint operator on a Hilbert space $H$ over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. Then $T$ has an eigenvalue $\mu \in \mathbb{K}$ with $\mu \neq 0$ and $|\mu| = \|T\|$, where $\|T\|$ is the operator norm of $T$.

results.title: A nonzero compact self-adjoint operator has a real eigenvalue of modulus equal to its norm, with a unit eigenvector
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A nonzero compact self-adjoint operator has a real eigenvalue of modulus equal to its norm, with a unit eigenvector. Let $T \neq 0$ be a compact self-adjoint operator on a Hilbert space $H$ over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. Then there are a real number $r$ and a unit vector $u \in H$ with $T u = r u$ and $|r| = \|T\|$, where $\|T\|$ is the operator norm of $T$.

results.title: Deflation step
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $T$ be a compact self-adjoint operator on a Hilbert space $H$ over $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $S$ be a linear subspace of $H$ that admits an orthogonal projection $P : H \to H$ onto $S$ and satisfies $T(S) \subseteq S$, and let $T_1 = PTP$ be the compression of $T$ to $S$. If $T_1 \neq 0$, then there are a real number $r$ and a unit vector $v \in S$ with $Tv = rv$, $|r| = \|T_1\|$ and $|r| \le \|T\|$.

results.title: Next eigenvalue after a finite family of eigenvectors

If $Tz \neq 0$ for some $z \in S$, then there are a real number $r$ and a unit vector $v$ with $\langle v, u_i \rangle = 0$ for every…

results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $T$ be a compact self-adjoint operator on a Hilbert space $H$ over $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. For every $\varepsilon > 0$ there is a bounded self-adjoint operator $F$ on $H$ with finite-dimensional range such that $\|T - F\| \le \varepsilon$.

results.title: Binomial random subset
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a type $X$ and $p \in [0, 1]$, the binomial random subset distribution on $X$ with parameter $p$ is the probability measure on the subsets of $X$ under which each element of $X$ belongs to the random subset independently with probability $p$. results.title: $p$-small families of sets
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $X$ be a finite type and $p \in [0, 1]$. A family $\mathcal{F}$ of subsets of $X$ is $p$-small when there is a family $\mathcal{G}$ of subsets of $X$ such that every member of $\mathcal{F}$ contains some member of $\mathcal{G}$ and $\sum_{S \in \mathcal{G}} p^{|S|} \le 1/2$.

results.title: $k$-strings
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: For a natural number $k$, a $k$-string is a finite sequence (possibly empty) of elements of $\{0, 1, \ldots, k-1\}$.

results.title: The reverse-permute relation
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $k$, a $k$-string $s$ is related to a $k$-string $t$ by the reverse-permute (RP) relation when there is a permutation $\sigma$ of $\{0, 1, \ldots, k-1\}$ such that $t$ is obtained, either from $s$ or from the reversal of $s$, by replacing each entry $x$ with $\sigma(x)$.

results.title: Rewriting rules
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: A rewriting rule over an alphabet $\alpha$ is a pair $(l, r)$ of words over $\alpha$; applying it replaces an occurrence of $l$ by $r$.

results.title: One-step rewriting
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: Let $R$ be a string rewriting system, given as a list of rules. A word $w$ rewrites to a word $w'$ in one step of $R$ when there are a rule $(l, r)$ of $R$ and words $u$ and $v$ with $w = u l v$ and $w' = u r v$.

results.title: Derivations in a string rewriting system
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a list of rules $R$, a word $x$ derives a word $y$ when $x$ rewrites to $y$ in zero or more steps of $R$, that is, when $(x, y)$ lies in the reflexive-transitive closure of the one-step rewriting relation of $R$.

results.title: The reachability problem for string rewriting
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An instance $(R, x, y)$ consists of a string rewriting system $R$, given as a list of rules, and two words $x$ and $y$; it is a yes-instance of the reachability problem when $x$ rewrites to $y$ in zero or more steps of $R$.

results.title: Rewriting systems with nonempty sides
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A string rewriting system $R$, given as a list of rules $(l, r)$, has nonempty sides when every rule of $R$ has a nonempty left side $l$ and a nonempty right side $r$.

results.title: Lifting a word to the extended alphabet
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: A word $a_1 \cdots a_n$ over $\alpha$ is sent to the word $a_1 \cdots a_n$ over the extended alphabet of $\alpha$ in which each $a_i$ is read as a letter.

results.title: The start domino of the reduction from reachability to MPCP
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $x$ be a word over an alphabet $\alpha$, and extend $\alpha$ by a star $\star$ and an end marker $\diamond$. The start domino of $x$ has top the one-letter word $\diamond$ and bottom the word $\diamond x \star$, with the letters of $x$ read as letters of the extended alphabet.

results.title: Final domino
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a word $y$ over $\alpha$, the final domino of $y$ is the domino over the extended alphabet with top $y \star \diamond$ and bottom $\diamond$, where $y$ is read as a word of letters, $\star$ is the row separator and $\diamond$ is the end marker.

results.title: The separator domino
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Over the extended alphabet, that is, an alphabet $\alpha$ together with a star $\star$ and an end marker $\diamond$, the separator domino has top and bottom both equal to the one-letter word $\star$; the star separates the rows of a derivation.

results.title: The domino of a rewriting rule
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a rule $(l, r)$ over an alphabet $\alpha$, the domino of the rule has top $l$ and bottom $r$, read as words over the extended alphabet, that is, $\alpha$ together with a star and an end marker.

results.title: Copy domino
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a letter $a$ of $\alpha$, the copy domino of $a$ is the domino over the extended alphabet whose top and bottom are both the one-letter word $a$.

results.title: Letters of a rewriting instance
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an instance $(R, x, y)$ of the reachability problem, where $R = [(l_1, r_1), \dots, (l_k, r_k)]$ is a list of rewriting rules and $x$, $y$ are words, the letters of the instance form the word $l_1 r_1 l_2 r_2 \cdots l_k r_k \, x \, y$, a list in which a letter may occur several times.

results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $(R, x, y)$ be an instance of the reachability problem over an alphabet $\alpha$, where $R = [(l_1, r_1), \dots, (l_k, r_k)]$, and write $\#$ for the separator and $\diamond$ for the end marker of the extended alphabet $\mathrm{Sym}(\alpha)$, in which letters of $\alpha$ are read as letters. Let $a_1 \cdots a_m$ be the word $l_1 r_1 l_2 r_2 \cdots l_k r_k \, x \, y$, the letters of the instance. The MPCP…

results.title: Letters differ from the star
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every letter $a$ of the alphabet $\alpha$, the symbol $a$ of the extended alphabet of the MPCP-to-PCP reduction is different from the star $\star$.

results.title: Comparing words of letters before a separator
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $u, v$ be words over $\alpha$, read as words of letters, and let $X, Y$ be words over the extended alphabet of $\alpha$. If $u X = v \star Y$, where $\star$ is the row separator, then there is a word $w$ over $\alpha$ with $v = u w$ and $X = w \star Y$.

results.title: The backward direction of the MPCP reduction
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $(R, x, y)$ be a reachability instance and read words over $\alpha$ as words of letters. Let $A$ be a sequence of dominoes of the MPCP instance of $(R, x, y)$. For all words $v, s, t$ over $\alpha$, if $s$ rewrites to $t$ under $R$ in zero or more steps and the top of $A$ equals $v \star t$ followed by the bottom of $A$, where $\star$ is the row separator, then $s v$ rewrites to $y$ under $R$ in zero or more…

results.title: Rewriting steps keep the letters of the instance
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $(R, x, y)$ be an instance of the reachability problem over an alphabet $\alpha$. If a word $w$ rewrites to a word $w'$ in one step of $R$ and every letter of $w$ is among the letters of the instance, then every letter of $w'$ is among the letters of the instance.

results.title: The forward direction of the MPCP reduction
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $(R, x, y)$ be a reachability instance and read words over $\alpha$ as words of letters. If a word $w$ over $\alpha$ rewrites to $y$ under $R$ in zero or more steps and every letter of $w$ occurs in a rule of $R$, in $x$ or in $y$, then there is a sequence $A$ of dominoes of the MPCP instance of $(R, x, y)$ whose top is $w \star$ followed by the bottom of $A$, where $\star$ is the row separator.

results.title: Reachability reduces to MPCP
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For an instance $(R, x, y)$ of the reachability problem, $x$ rewrites to $y$ in zero or more steps of $R$ if and only if the MPCP instance of $(R, x, y)$ has an MPCP solution, that is, a solution that starts with its first domino.

results.title: The total reduction of reachability with nonempty sides to MPCP
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: On an instance $(R, x, y)$ of the reachability problem, the reduction returns the MPCP instance of $(R, x, y)$ when every rule of $R$ has a nonempty left side and a nonempty right side, and otherwise the empty list of dominoes, which has no solution.

results.title: The word problem of a Thue system
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: On an instance $(R, x, y)$, where $R$ is a list of rewriting rules and $x$, $y$ are words, the word problem asks whether $x$ and $y$ are related by the equivalence relation generated by the one-step rewriting relation of $R$, that is, by its reflexive, symmetric and transitive closure.

results.title: NS property
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A function $h : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ has the *NS property* if it is monotone (weakly increasing) and, for all $z, z' \in \mathbb{N}$ and every natural number $i \ge 1$, $\lfloor z / 2^i \rfloor = \lfloor z' / 2^i \rfloor$ implies $\lfloor h(z) / 2^{i-1} \rfloor = \lfloor h(z') / 2^{i-1} \rfloor$.

results.title: Constant functions have the NS property
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $c$, the constant function $\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ with value $c$ has the NS property.

results.title: The identity function lacks the NS property
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The identity function on the natural numbers does not have the NS property: $\lfloor 0/2 \rfloor = \lfloor 1/2 \rfloor$, but $0 \ne 1$.

results.title: Constant extension preserves the NS property
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $z \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $h : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ satisfy $h(a) \le h(b)$ whenever $a \le b \le z$, and $\lfloor h(a) / 2^{i-1} \rfloor = \lfloor h(b) / 2^{i-1} \rfloor$ whenever $a, b \le z$, $i \ge 1$ and $\lfloor a / 2^i \rfloor = \lfloor b / 2^i \rfloor$. Then the function sending $x$ to $h(x)$ for $x \le z$ and to $h(z)$ for $x > z$ has the NS property.

results.title: Taking a minimum preserves quotients by powers of two
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $a, b, c, k \in \mathbb{N}$. If $\lfloor a / 2^k \rfloor = \lfloor b / 2^k \rfloor$, then $\lfloor \min(a, c) / 2^k \rfloor = \lfloor \min(b, c) / 2^k \rfloor$.

results.title: Quotients of a truncated NS function by powers of two
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $h : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ have the NS property and let $z, z', k \in \mathbb{N}$ with $k \ge 1$ and $\lfloor z' / 2^k \rfloor = \lfloor z / 2^k \rfloor$. Then for every $y \in \mathbb{N}$, $\lfloor \min(h(z'), y) / 2^{k-1} \rfloor = \lfloor \min(h(z), y) / 2^{k-1} \rfloor$.

results.title: Mex step for chocolate bars with one function
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $g : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ have the NS property, and let $x, z, c$ be natural numbers with $x \le g(z)$ and $c < x \oplus z$, where $\oplus$ is nim-sum (bitwise exclusive or). Then $c = u \oplus z$ for some $u < x$, or $c = \min(g(w), x) \oplus w$ for some $w < z$.

results.title: Mex step for chocolate bars with two functions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $g, h : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ have the NS property, and let $x, y, z, c$ be natural numbers with $x \le g(z)$, $y \le h(z)$ and $c < x \oplus y \oplus z$, where $\oplus$ is nim-sum (bitwise exclusive or). Then $c = u \oplus y \oplus z$ for some $u < x$, or $c = x \oplus v \oplus z$ for some $v < y$, or $c = \min(g(w), x) \oplus \min(h(w), y) \oplus w$ for some $w < z$.

Then either there are an index $i$ and some $u < x_i$ such that $c$ is the nim-sum $x_1 \oplus \cdots \oplus x_m \oplus z$ with $x_i$…

results.title: Nim-sum image identity for two NS functions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $g, h : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ have the NS property and let $x, y, z \in \mathbb{N}$ with $x \le g(z)$ and $y \le h(z)$. Writing $\oplus$ for the nim-sum (bitwise exclusive or) of natural numbers, the sets $\{x \oplus y \oplus w : w < z\}$ and $\{\min(g(w), x) \oplus \min(h(w), y) \oplus w : w < z\}$ are equal, where $w$ ranges over the natural numbers.

results.title: Nim-sum image identity for one NS function
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $g : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ have the NS property and let $x, z \in \mathbb{N}$ with $x \le g(z)$. Writing $\oplus$ for the nim-sum (bitwise exclusive or) of natural numbers, the sets $\{x \oplus w : w < z\}$ and $\{\min(g(w), x) \oplus w : w < z\}$ are equal, where $w$ ranges over the natural numbers.

results.title: Halving functions have the NS property
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $m \ge 1$, the function $x \mapsto \lfloor x / 2^m \rfloor$ on $\mathbb{N}$ has the NS property.

results.title: Equal quotients by a power of two lie in one dyadic block
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $i$ be a natural number and let $z < z'$ be natural numbers. Then $\lfloor z / 2^i \rfloor = \lfloor z' / 2^i \rfloor$ if and only if there is a natural number $d$ with $d \cdot 2^i \le z$ and $z' < (d + 1) \cdot 2^i$.

results.title: Dyadic splitting of two numbers with different quotients
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $z, z', i$ be natural numbers with $\lfloor z / 2^i \rfloor < \lfloor z' / 2^i \rfloor$. Then there are natural numbers $c$, $s$ and $t$ with $s \ge i$, $t < 2^s$, $z = c \cdot 2^{s+1} + t$ and $c \cdot 2^{s+1} + 2^s \le z'$.

results.title: Indicator functions with the NS property
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ be monotone, with $f(x) \le 1$ for all $x$ and $f(x) = 1$ for some $x$. Then $f$ has the NS property if and only if there is an even $m \in \mathbb{N}$ such that $f$ is the indicator function of $\{n \in \mathbb{N} : n \ge m\}$, that is, $f(n) = 1$ for $n \ge m$ and $f(n) = 0$ for $n < m$.

results.title: Pass indicator of Nim with a restricted pass
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For $s$ piles with thresholds $m_0, \dots, m_{s-1}$ and pile sizes $x_0, \dots, x_{s-1}$ (natural numbers), the pass indicator is $1$ if $m_j \le x_j$ for some pile $j$ (the pass may be used), and $0$ if $x_j < m_j$ for every pile $j$.

results.title: The Nim pass indicator is at most one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $s \in \mathbb{N}$ and all $m, x \in \mathbb{N}^s$, the pass indicator of $m$ at $x$ is at most $1$; that is, it takes values in $\{0, 1\}$.

results.title: The pass is unavailable from the empty position

results.title: Nim-sum Grundy numbers of chocolate bars with two functions
results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Nim-sum Grundy numbers of chocolate bars with four functions

results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $k$ be a natural number with $k \equiv 3 \pmod 4$, and let $F(w, x) = \lfloor (w + x) / k \rfloor$. For all $w, x, y \in \mathbb{N}$ with $y \le F(w, x)$, the three-dimensional chocolate bar $\mathrm{CB}(F, w, x, y)$ has Grundy number $0$ (is a P-position) if and only if $w \oplus x \oplus y = 0$, where $\oplus$ denotes nim-sum (bitwise exclusive or).
